A 1941 Chicago photo has left people scratching their heads after they spotted what appears to be a boy holding an 'iPad'

02:00 ET, 17 Sep 2026Updated 04:36 ET, 17 Sep 2026

A photograph dating back to 1941 has ignited fierce debate among observers who believe it might prove time travel is real.

‌

The historic image, taken by Edward Rosskam on Chicago's South Side, depicts a line of smartly dressed children and teenagers queuing outside a movie theater.

‌

However, one youngster at the frame's edge has left viewers puzzled. Social media users are now convinced the child is holding an Apple iPad.

Posted on Reddit's timetravelerscaught forum, one user commented: "iPad carrying moviegoer, all the way to the right."

Yet not everyone's convinced by the time-travel theory – with some suggesting it could be something much more mundane. "Looks like a book to me," one person commented, reports the Daily Star.

‌

Detailing old movie theater customs, another explained: "Back in the day of early film, ushers scanned the audience for pens and notepads as to prevent bootleg recreations of the film."

Another user said: "If I can time travel, have an iPad and I'm black why in God's name would I go to the South Side of Chicago in 1941 to watch a matinee of 'The Aldrich Family? !'".

‌

Others took the chance to reflect nostalgically on past times, with one person noting the attire visible in the photograph, saying: "They all are dressed so nicely. To wear your Sunday best to see the movies, it must have been a fantastic treat."

Another said: "Part of me wishes we would all dress up like that for the little things, and then I debate if I am even going to shower today."

Meanwhile, another user added: "Amazing how nicely dressed they all are. The little men's hats are so adorable."

‌

The post follows another woman's viral TikTok moment after she uncovered a photograph containing her lookalike.

Lindsay Bullis revealed she was exploring her family history online when she came across an image of a woman bearing the "same face" as hers.

The 28-year-old maintained she shared an "uncanny" likeness with Mary Beckwith, her great-great-great-great-grandmother on her father's side who lived between 1805 and 1873.

Posting side-by-side photos of herself next to Mary, Lindsay accumulated over 4.6 million views on her video and left audiences thoroughly persuaded she's travelled through time.
